hits.text: The door is open and inside the wall the agent can proceed, but the goal has not yet been reached. The only remaining objective is to step onto the goal tile, after which the task is complete. No further prerequisite remains since the door is already open.

The agent is standing on the exit but the box is not in hand, so the box still needs to be picked up. Once the box is held, the task is complete; if it falls instead, it must be recovered on the very next step. The exit has been reached, but the box requirement is not yet met.

The agent is on the exit and the box has just fallen with empty hands, so the box must be picked up immediately. If it is held on the next step the task is complete; otherwise the task fails. The exit is reached, but the carried-box requirement still hangs on the next step.

The box has just fallen on the same step the agent arrived at the exit, leaving the hands empty, so the recovery is still owed. If the agent is holding the box again on the very next move, the task is complete at the exit; otherwise the requirement is violated and success is no longer possible.

The agent has reached the exit but without the box in its hands. The box must now be picked up again, ideally on the very next move if it is still loose; once it is being carried, the task is complete. Failing to retrieve the box when the chance passes ends the episode in failure.

The agent has recovered or is otherwise holding the box on a step after a slip, with the pickup promise still owed one more confirmation step. If the box stays in hand through the next step, the task is complete; if it slips again on that step, the box must be picked up on the step after that or the attempt fails.

The agent has opened the locked door and entered the target room, but has not yet picked up the ball. The only remaining objective is to pick up the ball. If the agent is still holding the key, it must be dropped first because the key and ball cannot be carried together; once the ball is picked up, the mission is complete.

The door has been opened, so the requirement is satisfied whether the key was lost beforehand or not. Any obligation arising from losing the key early has been met. The task is complete as far as this rule is concerned, and no further action is required for it.

No requirement is pending right now: the agent either is not carrying the matching key or the door is already open. The task is satisfied and stays satisfied as long as the door gets opened whenever the key is in hand.

No client order is pending and the agent is not carrying food. Idle between clients: watch the counter for a client arrival (client_arrived moves to u1), and handle any siren separately. No food should be held at this point.

Idle between clients: no order is pending. Watch for a client to arrive at the counter (go to u1 and take the order) and be ready to chase any food that slips (go to u5); otherwise continue waiting or reposition near the counter.

Initial state: the matching key has not yet been seen. Explore the corridor and side rooms, looking through open doorways and into the left-column rooms to locate the key, while avoiding the locked target door. Once the key comes into view, progress moves to u1.
The matching key has been located but is not yet carried. Navigate to the key and pick it up to advance to u2; do not toggle the locked target door, which would end the run in the failure state.

Normal progress: the box is either in hand or was never lost, and no recovery is pending. Keep the box with you while heading to the exit. If the box falls this step, you enter recovery; stepping onto the exit while carrying it completes the task, while stepping onto the exit empty-handed fails it.

The agent is standing on the exit but not carrying the box, and the box did not fall on this step. To finish successfully, the agent must now pick the box up (or otherwise come to hold it) while still at the exit. If the box falls before it is held, the agent enters the pick-up obligation; if it picks the box up, the task is satisfied.
The door is not yet open. The only requirement is to get the locked door open, which in practice means obtaining the matching key and toggling the door; once the door is open the task is complete.

The agent has held the matching key on two distinct occasions, so the key requirement is already satisfied. The remaining objective is to pick up the mission's designated box, which still needs to be carried. Once the box is picked up, the task is complete.

The agent has carried the matching key on two distinct steps, satisfying the key-holding requirement. The target box is still in the other room and must be picked up to finish; once the box is taken, the task is complete.
The ball has been moved away, the door is open, the key is not held, and the box is being carried. All requirements are satisfied and the task is complete.
The ball has been moved away, the key is held, the door is open, and the box is being carried. All requirements are satisfied and the task is complete.

The agent has located the key and is carrying the ball, but the locked door is currently not open. It must reopen the locked door; once the door is open again, holding the ball satisfies the remaining requirements and the task is complete.

The agent has located the matching key and is carrying the ball, but the locked target door is still closed. The remaining objective is to open the locked door, after which the task is complete. Since the ball is held, the key cannot be carried, so the agent must put the ball down to handle the key and then retrieve the ball.

The key was found and the ball has been picked up, but because of the promise to open the locked door, the task does not finish until that door has been opened. The only remaining objective is to open the locked door guarding the target room; once it opens, the task is complete.

The door, which had already been opened, was subsequently closed while the matching key was in hand, and the target box is still uncollected. This creates a pending requirement to open the door again; reopening it restores normal progress toward the box. If the box is picked while the door remains shut, completion is still pending and the door must be opened afterward.

This is successful completion: the target box has been picked up after the matching key was acquired and the door had been opened. The required ordering and the key-holding obligation have been satisfied, including any need to reopen the door. No further action is needed.

The target box has been picked up, but the door is shut and an earlier time holding the matching key while the door was closed has not yet been followed by reopening it. That outstanding key-use requirement means the task is not complete yet. Opening the door is the final condition; once it is open, all requirements are satisfied.
